commands.review_summary:
The PR removes the macOS LaunchAgent restart pre-kickstart port-busy failure and updates launchd regression tests to allow `kickstart -k` while the gateway port is busy.

PR surface: Source -6, Tests -19. Total -25 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. for the intended managed-listener case: the PR supplies a real macOS LaunchAgent transcript and focused regression coverage. The unrelated-port and direct-caller failure mode is source-reproducible from the removed guard, but was not independently executed in this review.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] The remaining blocker is the maintainer-owned lifecycle contract for unrelated port owners and direct restart callers, not a safe mechanical repair.

target.title: fix: allow macOS gateway restart while LaunchAgent owns its port
target.body:
Related: #88309

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, `openclaw gateway restart` can fail before launchd is ever asked to restart the gateway when the configured port is still busy after stale-process cleanup.

That is a valid and common state for a managed LaunchAgent: the currently running gateway owns the port, or launchd's `KeepAlive` policy has already replaced it during the cleanup window. The previous restart path treated any remaining listener as a fatal precondition and threw before `launchctl enable` or `launchctl kickstart -k`. As a result, an explicit restart request could reject a healthy, launchd-managed service without invoking the operation designed to replace it.

The invalid guard is still present on [current `main` before this patch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0ac7b24d56ca739ce3c2291523206ba04c2fbefe/src/daemon/launchd.ts#L1335-L1347) and in the latest release, [v2026.7.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.7.1/src/daemon/launchd.ts). The broader #88309 also covers SIGTERM intent and in-process restart handoff behavior; this PR intentionally fixes only the still-reproducible external/direct LaunchAgent restart branch and therefore uses `Related`, not `Closes`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The patch keeps the existing effective-port resolution and `cleanStaleGatewayProcessesSync(cleanupPort)`, but removes the second, generic port inspection and fatal throw before launchd replacement. The normal path then continues through the existing plist rewrite, service enable, `kickstart -k`, unloaded-service bootstrap fallback, mutation audit, and error propagation.

This is the right boundary for the fix for the following reasons:

- **It matches launchd's replacement contract.** macOS documents `launchctl kickstart -k` as terminating the service if it is already running and starting it again. Requiring the running service's port to be free before invoking that command contradicts the operation's purpose.
- **A free-port precondition is racy under `KeepAlive`.** Even if cleanup briefly releases the socket, launchd may immediately respawn the managed gateway before the next inspection. Waiting longer or repeating the same check cannot create a stable invariant; a healthy managed service may legitimately keep the port continuously occupied.
- **Targeted stale cleanup remains in place.** `cleanStaleGatewayProcessesSync` identifies OpenClaw gateway processes by process arguments, excludes the caller and its ancestors, terminates verified stale listeners, and performs its existing bounded port-release poll. This PR does not kill arbitrary port owners or remove stale-process protection.
- **Stop and restart retain different postconditions.** `openclaw gateway stop` still calls `assertGatewayPortReleasedAfterStop`, polls for release, and fails if the port remains busy. A stop must end with no listener. A restart must end with a healthy replacement, not with an observable instant when no process owns the socket.
- **Failures are not swallowed.** Existing `enable`, `bootout`, `bootstrap`, and `kickstart` errors still propagate. The normal CLI restart flow still calls `waitForGatewayHealthyRestart`, so an unrelated port conflict or a replacement that never becomes healthy is reported after launchd has had the opportunity to perform the requested restart.
- **Direct service callers keep the existing supervisor-operation contract.** Some internal callers invoke `service.restart` without the CLI's readiness wrapper. If readiness should become part of every direct caller's contract, that is a broader, cross-platform service API decision. Retaining a racy “port was free once before restart” check would not prove that the replacement became healthy.
- **Booting the service out unconditionally is a larger and riskier semantic change.** The current code uses `bootout`/`bootstrap` only when a plist reload is required; otherwise `kickstart -k` is the intended lower-downtime replacement path. This PR preserves that split and the existing detached in-process handoff path.
- **Other platforms are intentionally unchanged.** systemd delegates replacement to `systemctl restart`; Windows has a separate Scheduled Task end/run flow. Their supervisor contracts do not justify imposing a macOS precondition that launchd itself does not require.

The resulting source change is deliberately small: it removes one invalid precondition while leaving service identity, configuration, authentication, protocol, persistence, and non-macOS behavior untouched.

## User Impact

For users running the gateway as a macOS LaunchAgent, an explicit restart can now reach launchd even when the active or immediately respawned managed gateway still owns the configured port. The command no longer fails solely because the service it is replacing is alive.

The user-visible safety properties remain:

- normal CLI restarts still wait for a healthy gateway and report readiness failures;
- launchctl mutation failures still surface;
- stop still verifies that the port is released;
- stale OpenClaw gateway cleanup still runs;
- in-process restart handoff, plist reload behavior, Linux, and Windows are unchanged.

No configuration migration, API change, dependency change, new permission, or security-sensitive data handling is introduced.

## Evidence

### launchd contract and current-source proof

On the macOS host used for validation:

```console
$ launchctl help kickstart
Usage: launchctl kickstart [-k] [-p] <service-target>
        -k      Terminates the service if it is already running.
```

The rebased patch is based on `main` commit [0ac7b24d56ca](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0ac7b24d56ca739ce3c2291523206ba04c2fbefe). Its regression test exercises the exact invariant: with the gateway port mocked as busy, restart still runs stale cleanup, does not call the generic inspection gate, returns `{ outcome: "completed" }`, and invokes:

```text
launchctl enable gui/<uid>/ai.openclaw.gateway
launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/ai.openclaw.gateway
```

The rebase also preserves current-main coverage for resolving the final repeated LaunchAgent `--port` flag before cleanup.

### Live macOS LaunchAgent proof

The original behavior proof was run in a real macOS launchd user session on June 1, 2026, using disposable profile `pr89096proof`, LaunchAgent `ai.openclaw.pr89096proof`, and port `19896`. The proof profile used loopback `gateway.auth.mode=none` only so the published health output contained no secret.

The proof head was `601a254812234921b0bd394c66691dfb39e56e82`; the behavior-changing source edit is unchanged by the current-main rebase.

Before restart, the LaunchAgent was loaded, running, and owned both loopback listeners:

```console
$ launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/ai.openclaw.pr89096proof
state = running
arguments = {
  /opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node
  /Users/shawn/Dev/openclaw/dist/index.js
  gateway
  --port
  19896
}
pid = 68831

$ lsof -nP -iTCP:19896 -sTCP:LISTEN
COMMAND   PID  USER   FD   TYPE DEVICE SIZE/OFF NODE NAME
node    68831 shawn   18u  IPv4  ...       0t0  TCP 127.0.0.1:19896 (LISTEN)
node    68831 shawn   19u  IPv6  ...       0t0  TCP [::1]:19896 (LISTEN)
```

The patched restart reached launchd instead of failing on the expected busy port:

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs --profile pr89096proof gateway restart
[restart] killing 1 stale gateway process(es) before restart: 68831
Restarted LaunchAgent: gui/501/ai.openclaw.pr89096proof
```

Afterward, launchd had replaced PID `68831` with PID `69148` on the same port, and both the deep connectivity and health probes passed:

```console
$ launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/ai.openclaw.pr89096proof
state = running
runs = 7
pid = 69148
last terminating signal = Terminated: 15

$ node openclaw.mjs --profile pr89096proof gateway status --deep
Service: LaunchAgent (loaded)
Runtime: running (pid 69148, state active)
Recent restart handoff: full-process via launchd; source=operator-restart; reason=gateway.restart; pid=68831
Connectivity probe: ok
Listening: 127.0.0.1:19896, [::1]:19896

$ node openclaw.mjs --profile pr89096proof gateway health --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "eventLoop": {
    "degraded": false,
    "reasons": []
  },
  "plugins": {
    "errors": []
  }
}
```

### Validation

The original macOS proof head passed:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`
- `pnpm test:macos:ci`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm build`

The current rebased head, `ec7dbdc7026c4944134a8dd71a3780b1fde2875e`, passes under Node 24.18.0:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts` — 110 tests passed
- `pnpm test:macos:ci` — 227 tests passed across five Vitest shards
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/launchd.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/daemon/launchd.ts src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

The immediately preceding, patch-identical head completed GitHub Actions with 77 passing jobs and 35 intentional path/matrix skips before this final disjoint main rebase. On that head, the required [`Real behavior proof`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29738020118/job/88337871916), security, dependency, lint, type, build, smoke, and all other runnable checks passed.

Two primary shards are red in unchanged test surfaces; [`openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29738021499/job/88339112091) is red only because it aggregates them:

- [`checks-node-compact-small-1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29738021499/job/88337969110) failed in the unchanged `test/scripts/pr-wrappers.test.ts` fixture (`expected 1 to be 0`). The exact suite passes locally under Node 24.18.0 (12/12), and the [matching shard passed on the successful immediately preceding base-main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29737189848/job/88335411116).
- [`checks-node-compact-large-2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29738021499/job/88337969133) failed when the unchanged `src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.test.ts` fixture hit `ENOTEMPTY` while deleting its temporary directory. The exact test passes locally under Node 24.18.0 (11/11), and the [matching shard passed on the successful immediately preceding base-main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29737189848/job/88335411102).

Both failures are isolated from this patch: the PR changes only `src/daemon/launchd.ts` and `src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`; the failing files and their implementation surfaces are byte-for-byte unchanged from base `0ac7b24d56ca739ce3c2291523206ba04c2fbefe`. External contributors do not have the repository-admin permission GitHub requires to rerun failed upstream jobs in place.

AI-assisted: Codex was used to audit the current source, callers, tests, platform contracts, and relevant history; reconcile the rebase; and draft this explanation. The implementation claims above are backed by the linked source, regression coverage, launchctl help text, and terminal behavior proof.
